function: above_phy (pp. 3, 6): a learned GCNN branching policy (REINFORCE) speeds up branch-and-bound for multi-BS ISAC task allocation, i.e. binary BS-user association and BS-target sensing scheduling per time slot.
notes: Exclusion reason above_phy. The learning solves task allocation, which is user association and scheduling. p. 3: "to indicate if the u-th user is associated with the b-th BS at the n-th time slot" and "indicates if the b-th BS is sensing the t-th target in the n-th time slot"; p. 3: "we consider time-slotted scheduling"; p. 6: "are the optimization design variables" (only these binary association and sensing variables). The learned element is a GCNN brancher inside branch-and-bound. p. 6: "The action at each state is the index of the branching variable"; p. 10: "we adopt a plain REINFORCE [29] as our RL algorithm to train the GCNN enabled brancher". No physical-layer decision is learned jointly with the allocation. The DFRC beamformer is classical. p. 5: "obtain the DFRC beamformer fD,btu via beampattern synthesis", solved by "the Riemannian manifold based steepest gradient descent (RMSGD) algorithm". The sensing beamformer is "set to the steering vector" (p. 5), and the communication beamformer "can be determined based on hbu" (p. 4). Borderline, for the reviewer: (a) the allocation of BS beams to sensing and communication tasks could be read as ISAC resources, which would make it area 5 (title p. 1: "Efficient Task Allocation"; index terms: "resource allocation, multi-BS collaboration"); (b) the brancher only speeds up an exact solver (p. 10: "the optimality of our solution can be guaranteed"). All reported results (Figs. 3-10, pp. 10-13) compare allocation schemes, and the main text has no runtime comparison of the learned brancher against plain B&B. That could also support no_learning. I chose above_phy because GCRL presents the learning as part of its method. If the reviewer included the work, the system and results checks pass: 4 BSs with Nt = 16 antennas, 3 single-antenna users, 30 GHz, simulation results (p. 10).
